utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. I expect Mr. Piletta-Zanin to be back in a second, but I thought we could perhaps already start with Mr. Kovacs. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Prosecution has requested to deal with the documents to be tendered during the examination of the last witness after the return of Mr. Ierace. So we will deal with that in due course. May I take it that the Prosecution is ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, I have so been informed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam usher can you please escort the witness into the courtroom. I take it it is Mr. Kovacs

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think the Court has already been informed but there would be the name for a Hungarian interpreter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We were informed about that and it is the same interpreter that assisted the last Dutch witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very versatile.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kovacs, I take it. Before giving testimony in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text of the solemn declaration will be handed out to the interpreter. If you understand and can speak enough English to do it in the English language, fine. If not, we will ask the interpreter to translate it for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Dr. Kovacs. Ms. Bodor, you made already the solemn declaration during the testimony of the last witness. May I then remind you, that you are still bound by the declaration you gave when translating for General Van Baal. Then there is no need to repeat that. Please be seated. Please be seated. When Mr. Stamp has restructured his desk, he may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: My apologies for the disturbance. Examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Colonel. Colonel, I am going to ask you to take whatever documents you brought away from in front of you from the time being. Is your name -- or could you please tell us your name, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is asking me whether the interpreter will take his interpretation directly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Vilmos Kovacs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't understand. Ms. Bodor, I didn't understand the last question. You said it was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness was asking me whether he could speak now. He was asking a question to the translator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now better do understand what you meant. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Kovac --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Dr. Kovacs are you able to read and understand English to some degree?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: I can read English and I understand some English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, I ask that he be handed a copy of the report filed on the 14th of May and it is now designated Exhibit P3725.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me, please. The witness would like to hear his own interpretation and apparently the headset is not working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The headset is not working. On what channel are we? In what language would he like to hear his words being interpreted?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In Hungarian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether we provide for that. If he speaks Hungarian, it will be translated in another language. But when he speaks English, he is speaking one of the official languages of the Tribunal. Since the Hungarian translation would only, for the benefit of the witness, and would not be put down apart from -- not even on the -- not even on the live channel. Yes. Please proceed. If there is any difficulty. If you say when English words or used or if you want to express yourself in English or even French, if you have any doubt on whether you do understand or whether you express yourself in the right way, please ask for the assistance of the interpreters or my intervention, if necessary. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Kovacs, I see you have taken the opportunity to peruse a document that has just been handed. Have you had an opportunity before now to peruse a copy of that English document?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, I have had the opportunity to look through the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it contain a one-page resume of your training and experience in artillery matters including the purpose effectiveness and operation of artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Do you mean the first page?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have. I have seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that first page, does it contain thereafter your report translated into English, from Hungarian into English?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. I have read through the document which is in front of me at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having read through it, are there any changes which you would like to make to make the document more completely accurate?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. I think that a few changes are necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President and Your Honours, may I quickly go through that aspect?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, one thing only. Could we have -- I do not think we have this document which was distributed. Could we have it in Hungarian, that is, a copy with the author's signature, with the witness's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I can make a copy available to my friends at the next break. I must confess that I have never used the Hungarian copy. We filed the English copy and I am in the process now of having it authenticated, the document which was filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You seek to tender the English version of the document and not any Hungarian.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether the signature would then still be relevant, but if you would like, you can get a copy from the Prosecution during the next break. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you have a look at page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Line 16 of page 3 which begins with the word, "light."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything about that line which you would ask to change?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to change it because I think this was probably a misprint or typing error rather. The correct figure is 105 millimetre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the same page, the 8th line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I am sorry, Mr. Stamp. Could you read the line as it is after the amendment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am grateful, Your Honour. I think that would be more precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it from your last answer that the line would read: "Light 37 to 105 millimetre."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, if you will, have a look at the 8th line counting from the bottom of the said page.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything that you would like to change in that line?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. I think there was a problem with the translation here. Bazooka as a word is not correct. I would like to change it for anti-tank guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, therefore the sentence would read, I take it from the number 2 on the page: "Choosing the most appropriate devise for the demolition of the target, which includes the type of artillery device that was involved in elimination of the target, with a field artillery cannon, Howitzer, mortar, or anti-aircraft gun."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Anti-tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks for the correction, Dr. Kovacs. Could you have a look at page 4 and the 10th, as well as the 11th line of that page. Is there anything about those lines which you would like to change?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: The correct term in this case could be "direct and indirect fire." Divided aiming should be replaced by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I have some technical difficulties because I am trying to listen to a channel, read the transcript and help my colleague who is following Serbian. And I am afraid that there is some problem. But every time you give a reference to a document, could you do that also refer to the document in Serbian so that Mr. -- So that General Galic could also follow, find immediately the line that you are talking about and also check it. And thank you very much in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it please you, Mr. President, and Your Honours, I am not sure I will be able to do that. But I will do my best to assist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we are speaking about page 4 in the English version the third paragraph of that page. I take it from your last answer that the section or the paragraph would read: "The artillery cannon accomplished the demolition of the targets with direct or indirect fire. During the direct aimed fire, the target is visible from the cannon with optical sights. Indirect fire is used when the target is not visible from the cannon." Is that how it reads?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: That's right. It is correct like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you look in the fourth paragraph of the same page 4 in the penultimate sentence, perhaps it is easier if I read it in English. "This is the most commonly used and most basic type of fuse and is applied to fragmentation shells and mine mortars." That is how it reads. Is there anything you would like to add to there?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to change the following: The last term of the sentence should be replaced by "projectiles or shells."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the "last term of the sentence," do you mean the last word of the sentence?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, the last two words of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For clarification, may I read it to you with this alteration. "This is a most commonly used and the most basic type of fuse and is applied to fragmentation shells and mortar shells or mortar projectiles."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, this is perfect like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the same page, could you have a look at the 11th line from the bottom and that is a line beginning with the word, "projectiles." Is there anything on that line, on the 11th line --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the Prosecution does not quote us the text in Serbian, we need a short pause so that General Galic can locate it. I am looking to my right, but I cannot also look at my back and work at my back. So could you please slow down and thank you very much in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that it is on page 4, approximately just under the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We found it, but I am not quite sure that General Galic can keep up at this speed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think we could now proceed. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything on that line which you would like to change or do you think it can remain the same?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: I would like to change something in the sentence. Namely, the term which concerns the fuse and I would like to change it for "delayed fuse" and I would like to replace "delayed fuse" with "time fuse," because this is the correct term.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would please have a look at page 5. Or before we get to page 5, may I just read that sentence just to confirm the alteration. And I take it now that it should read "Projectiles assembled with timed fuses are used for the destruction of troops, field and permanent offensive structures and buildings."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know so that we do not have to repeat it over and over again, I think that "fuse" actually means rather "detonateur" than "fusee". This is my humble opinion. If that is correct, would you please take note of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes this is a matter of translation English/French in a very technical matter which I could not -- so the, I take it, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, your suggestion is whether the French interpreters with the English/French interpretation would consider fuses to be translated as "detonateur". Yes, if from your professional point of view you would agree, I take it, it would be done. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take you now, Dr. Kovacs, to the 5th line of the 5th page. The sentence beginning with these words: "Projectiles assembled with delayed fuses are used primarily against." And that is the first line. Is there anything in that sentence which you would like to change?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you found it? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, similarly to the previous change, "time fuse" is the correct term instead of "delayed fuse."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it now the sentence would read: "Projectiles assembled with time fuses are used primarily" and it goes on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it that it is on page 4 for you, the 6th line -- the 5th line from the bottom. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the same page, on the 16th line counting from the bottom of the page, there is a sentence starting out "A delayed shell exploding above a target appears," and it goes on. Is there anything about that line that you would like to change?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, there is. I would like to replace "delayed shell" by "time-fused shell."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that it is line 16, page 5, for the Defence. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And therefore the start of the sentence should read: "A time-fused shell exploding above the target appears" and so on.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, perfect like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could now, sir, take you to page 10 and line 6 thereof. Is there anything in that line would you would ask to change?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we please give time for the Defence to find this because --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Six. Is it from the top or from the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything in that line that you would ask to change, sir?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, there is. Just like we changed the term previously. Here again "delayed fuse" must be replaced by "time fuse." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And therefore the sentence would read or would start: "Illumination rounds are activated with delayed fuses during the descending," and it goes on --

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: That is correct. "Delayed fuse" is the wrong term.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am grateful for the assistance. The sentence would read: "Illumination" rounds are activated with time fuses during the descending part of the trajectory."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: It is correct like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look now on the same page, 10 lines up from the bottom of the page. Is there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it is page 8, seventh line from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have it, Mr. President. But directly speaking, if Mr. Stamp could also just tell us the very first words of the sentence, that would really save us a lot of time for the future. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 10, 10 lines up from the bottom, the very first words being "by shooting illumination." Is there anything in that sentence that you would ask to change?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, there is. At the end of the sentence after "and." The very last answer, "...and also to disturb their armour piercing projectiles." This is not correct so we have to take this bit out of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What bit? If you could quote it exactly what should be taken out.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: "...and also to disturb their armour piercing projectiles."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what should it be replaced with?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: The last word of the sentence would be "instruments" and then full stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, I am not sure that I understood. I must admit it says the very last answer, and I am not sure what it actually means. Is that an erroneous usage or is that an "and" that was written as answer? So could please the witness repeat so that we can have a clarification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it is not replaced. The part taken out is not replaced by any words. So the last part of the sentence would just be deleted. I hear the witness confirms this. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. But I did not understand what it said in the transcript, line 21. What was it referring to in terms of saying "the very last answer." So that is what I was saying. This is line 21 of page 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness was referring to the last part of the answer, of the line. I think there is no confusion. He wants to take out that part. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I may, for clarification, re-read or read the sentence in accordance with your instructions: "By shooting illumination rounds, it is also possible to blind enemies observation posts and electro-optical instruments."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, if you will, have a look at page 12 and the 15th line from the top beginning with "Apply the most accurate procedure."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it everyone found it. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The line as it is now reads, "Apply the most accurate procedure determining the elements of the effective fire." Is there anything about that line which you would like to change?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, there is. There is a word in the sentence. "Effective fire." I would like to replace "effective" by "artillery fire."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now have a look at page 16. The second line on that page, the sentence beginning, "A 2 gram piece of shrapnel is sufficient to kill a man."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. There is one thing I would like to change in this sentence as well. I would like to replace "shrapnel" by "fragmentation effect". I am sorry. I think we don't need "effect" in this case. We just need "fragmentation".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words the sentence would read: "A 2 gram piece of fragmentation is sufficient to kill a man."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. This is going to be correct like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I could perhaps move on, Mr. President, Your Honours. I don't know if I could perhaps ask the witness -- I don't think it would be leading I will proceed to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you use the word "fragment" instead of "fragmentation"?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: In this sentence, the most important thing is that even "a 2 gram piece of fragment is capable of killing." This is the correct version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So it could therefore read: "A 2 gram piece of fragment is sufficient to kill a man"?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 6th line from the top of that page, the line beginning with the word, "increased," and reads on "since the shrapnel may bounce up or ricochet." Is there anything about that line that you would like to change?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, there is. In this sentence too, "shrapnel" should be replaced by "fragment".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you now have a look at page 22, the 5th line up from the bottom reading "120 millimetre M-75, etc." Is there anything that should be changed there?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, here again I would like to change something. There is a problem here. Because there are two similar types of launchers, M-75 and M-74. And since we are talking about launchers, the "M-74" is missing from the text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This 120 millimetre M-74 or M-75, is it a launcher or is it a mortar?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President I apologise, but this is not a problem with interpretation, although there is an interference with the microphones so the French booth was not able to get the translation, so I don't know whether they were not able to interpret it. I don't know what is the problem, but I believe that the microphone of the English booth is open. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, you have been asked to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I instead, rephrase it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you want to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the 120 millimetre M-74 should also be there. Where should it be exactly on this page?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: I think it is the printing. I think it is in the wrong place. This is a printing error. Because we are talking about a mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us how that part of the page should read?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Naturally, there is a list of mortars here and there are three different sizes, if you like. And this is where we should add as number 4 the one that I have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which one is that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I -- do I -- do I understand well that you should follow 82 millimetres M-68?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, exactly. That's where it should be and it should be number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look finally at page 25. I beg your pardon. Not finally, almost finally. Page 25 line 6 from the top, the line reading: "One gun layer." Is there anything you would like to change about that line?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the term is not correct. According to Hungarian terminology, you should understand "a gun aimer." So the correct word would be "aimer".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it, therefore, the sentence would read: "One gun aimer."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I take you now to page 26, the first line of that page beginning with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think it is the same page, and we are talking about the 120 millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I believe, Your Honour, is correct. May I just confirm that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you look in the middle of page 25 under the word -- under the sentence in bold print 120 millimetre mortar, the sentence is "one gun layer." Is there anything there to be changed?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly as we have done previously. Here again and also in page 26, line 4, instead of "gun layer," we should say "gun aimer," which would be the correct terminology.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So both lines are the one that I referred you to and the one you just now referred us to should read "one gun aimer"?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am grateful for Your Honours perspicacity and I am guided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, still in order to assist the Prosecution, I believe that we can make the same remark mutandis mutandi at the bottom of page 24, we will find "gun layer." I don't want to disturb Mr. Stamp, but this is just to be absolutely clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I am also grateful to my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I take your attention to that, page 24, the penultimate line, you see the word, the expression, "gun layer." Can I take it that that should be, "gun aimer"?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. Everywhere in the text there should be "gun aimer," because this is the number one operator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you have a look at page 26, the first line of that page. Is there anything in that line, and that is the line beginning, "the commander," is there anything in that line that you would ask to change?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. A change should be made in the sentence as well because the word "cupola" when you are talking about military vehicles is not used and we use the word "turret" instead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which case I take it, Dr. Kovacs, the sentence should read, "the commander is located in the turret"?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I then take it that on the third line, not only on the fourth line of page 26, "gun layer" should also be "gun aimer".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, naturally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at page 28 and on the line at the number 1 where there is number 1 which reads: "Number of the assembly shop," is there anything there that you think ought to be changed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in order to understand this perfectly, the French booth just repeated the terms in English and did not translate them which is not what they are supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we are changing an English text, I can imagine that the interpreters, for the precise wording, are not translating in order to avoid any confusion. If you would need then later on for your better understanding the translation, I am quite sure that the interpreters first having done what they are supposed to do, then will certainly assist you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At number 1 on that page, the sentence reads: "Number of the assembly shop." Is there anything there you would like to change?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to complete it because it would be more precise if we put "workshop" instead of just "shop".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it it would read: "Number 1 of the assembly workshop."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you have a look at page 29, fifth line down, starting with the word, "assembly" and ending with the word, "shop".

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: We should make the same change as previously, and "workshop" would be the correct term.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore it would read, "year of the assembly and the number of the assembling base, workshop." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Back to page 28. As a part numbered 5 on that page, is there anything you would like to change?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. I think the correct solution would be to say, instead of "level", the word "degree."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would have that part reading 5, "weight degree of the projectile."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at 6 on the same page which reads, "6, mark of explosive smoke," is there anything that you would change? I am asking you to look at page 6 in the text in the middle of the page. Not at page 6. I beg your pardon. At item 6 in the text of page 28, it reads "6, mark of explosive smoke." Is there anything else you would like to change?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it would be more precise if we said "mark of explosive," and the word "smoke" should be removed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the --

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Deleted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The section would read: "6 mark of explosive," is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I am trying to assist the French booth. It is not audible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that the French booth cannot hear the translation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am being told, because I am following the channel, that there is a technical problem with the microphones. I don't know what it is about, but it has been going on throughout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will, from now on, follow the French text as well. [Interpretation] Are you able to follow the interpretation, the translation, or is there a technical problem which needs to be taken care of? [In English] Has the English booth heard the observation by the French booth, that is to put out the microphone once they --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the French -- could the English booth switch off the microphone as soon as they finished their interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will then proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the same page, same page, page 28, at item 7 in the text at the middle of that page, it reads, "7, mark of smoke forming materiel." I beg your pardon. Sorry. At item 8 in the middle of that page which reads, "8, index of projectile fuse," is there anything there you would ask to change?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: No, no, there is nothing to change.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am going to ask you to give us a clarification of what you mean in the first sentence of the last paragraph of the report. That is at page 30. It says here in English, "Finally, I state that the above study was prepared on the basis of the questions asked by a court of law and requires much background information." Could you clarify that, if you can, please?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I was asked to write the expert material and this request was transmitted to me by the Court, The Hague, the Tribunal. And I think the word "court of law" that you find in the text is not correct because it is not a court, in fact, but it is the Tribunal who are entrusted to me the writing of this particular report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask you what you mean by "Tribunal"? By "Tribunal" do you mean the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is quite a leading question, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will put the question to you. Did you understand that you drafted the report for the Office of the Prosecutor of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, this is not the way I understood my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you then explain to us, if it was not for the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been an expert concerning matters related to artillery materiel and for the International Tribunal in The Hague. And during the course of this work of expertise, I was in touch with the military office in charge of analysis. And it is for them Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that I prepared my expert opinion. And it is in the course of this work that I prepared the expert opinion that you have here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that there is no dispute between the parties that there is only the Department of Military Analysis in the Office of the Prosecutor in this Tribunal? I am looking to both parties. If the Defence has got one, although not being part of the Prosecution -- of the Tribunal. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is challenged. We have different. But the witness should be allowed to continue and tell us everything, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, may I ask you, did your office invite Mr. Kovacs to write this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Then this issue is dealt with sufficiently. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So with those corrections, is the document that you were handed an accurate record of your observations and is it your report?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. I think that if we take into account the corrections, the report is accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I quickly take you to one or two parts of that report and ask if you would elaborate a little bit more on what you have said there. Earlier you asked us to change the word, "shrapnel" to "fragment." Is there a distinction between fragment and shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, naturally, there is a difference. The effect of the fragment is -- in fact, when you use the word "shrapnel effect," that is an old terminology, and it was not intended for state of the art type of materiel. Shrapnel effect, in fact, is something that you can talk about when you have fragments which are manufactured, prepared, and are inserted into the body of the shell beforehand. I would like to emphasise it once again. So this is the type of ammunition that is linked to a previous period in history if you like; whereas, the fragment effect is a completely different mechanism and this takes place when you fire a shell and as a result of the fuse, the shell will somehow explode. And then the work of the explosives inside, if you like, will simply break apart the body of the shell and there will be thousands and thousands of fragments. And in reality, this is exactly what we are talking about in the present text. And this is the fragment effect of the shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to direct your attention to page 16 and 17 of the report in which you made certain references to fuses, types of fuses. Can I take it that a fuse is a part of the shell or a device attached to the shell which is used to detonate it or to cause it to explode?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. You understood it quite correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Because the fuse is -- in every time the fuse is part of the shell. And once the shell reaches the target, the fuse will trigger off the process of detonation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At page 16, the last paragraph there, reading on to page 17, the second paragraph there, you have given various times which may elapse between the contact of the shell with the target and the detonation. Now, are these times, time periods, standard for artillery and mortar rounds in general or are they merely an illustrative?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: The times mentioned in the text are an indication. You should not be considering them as something that would apply to every single fuse. There are three types of fuses that I wanted to explain here. And the time periods are the delay periods. And in this context and in this specific case they are indicative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it from that, that for various types of rounds or various individual types of rounds the manufactures may have set specific ranges of time periods for delay in detonation and that the figures you give are not to be sed to apply to every single artillery round?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, your interpretation is quite correct. There are -- there is a wide variety of artillery fuses. And it is always a question of the target that you want to hit and this is how you select the right kind of fuse. And there again, there are differences between different types of fuses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the course of your report you use the expression, "calculated norm." Sometimes you use the expression, "determined norm of ordnance." In particular, I'd like to take you to page 1 of the report. I think that is line 14, beginning with these words or may I just read the relevant passage that I wish to ask about. "With non-observable targets it is not possible to determine the accuracy of the fire. The calculated norm of ordnance must therefore be launched at these types of targets. If we consider the siege of a city, we may speak of observable targets, since the targets shot at should be easily visible with optical instruments. Had it not been so, the determined norm of ordnance should have been fired." And you say, "for example, at 400 metres with a 120 millimetre mine mortar, 100 shells need to be fired at a non-armoured single target."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also at page 8, the third line from the bottom, third line from the bottom beginning -- or if I may read it: "Meanwhile the targets and the impacts are continuously observed from the commanding observation post and it is deemed necessary. Corrections can be made between the series of shots according to the deviation from targets. On targets in cities that are easily observable from the mountains, it is usually recommended to use this procedure. If it happens that the target is not observable, the relevant battery or division must shoot a calculated quantity of projectiles until the required level of demolition is deemed to have been achieved." Could you briefly elaborate what is a calculated norm or a determined norm of ordnance in respect of unobserved targets? As brief as you can.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Of course, I will try to be as brief as possible. The calculated norm of ammunition that you can find in the text is a norm of ammunition which is calculated on the basis of mathematical methods and other methods as well, taking into consideration a wide range of aspects. This is how it is determined what kind of quantity of ammunition is needed for the various kinds of targets. This is a pre-calculated norm and the artillery commander receives this norm. I would like to emphasise the fact that this is used if the target cannot be observed from the land, from an observation point in the land or the terrain, if you like. Because this requires quite a large quantity of ammunition. And the observability of the target, as regards the fact of ammunition, is a much better solution and a much economic solution as well. Obviously, this can only be used when the target is visible from this post in the terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said it is something which is pre-calculated and is contained in the text in respect to that type of fire. Can I ask you this question: In combat in cities where it is known that there resides a large civilian population, can you comment or express an opinion on the applicability of firing this calculated quantity or large amounts of projectiles at unobserved targets?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I will try to do my best. I think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there is a very big difference, at least in the Defence point of view, if "non-observable" and the target, "not observed," "non-observable and non-observed targets." Because when one says "non-observable," it does not mean that it is a not observed target. According to this report, here it is mentioned, "the non-observable targets," and I am saying that it could -- that I do not think that it is a merely a somatical point of view. There is a major difference between these two terms and we shall see that later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, I think it is something that can be asked about. It is merely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question is about non-observed targets. And that is the question. That could be targets that could not be observed or have not been observed, which is, of course, not the same. But if you would like to make this difference, you could have done this in cross-examination. Yes. The question --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But what I am trying to say is that the expert has throughout spoken about a non-observable target and now he is being asked to comment on something about a non-observed target and these two things are not the same and that is what I am trying to indicate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... not be observed? Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Kovacs, there are some targets, I take it, which cannot be observed using eyesight or optical instruments or any other method?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. The category of non-observable targets includes targets which cannot be observed respecting the type of the fire which is supposed to be fired or the type of the target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The question I am asking about refers to targets which are not being observed and I repeat it: In combats -- in combat in cities where it is known that there resides a large civilian population, can you comment or express an opinion on the applicability of firing this calculated quantity of large amounts of projectiles at targets which are not observed?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: I can express an opinion about that in general terms, because the question was a very precise question. You always have to take into consideration the actual conditions. However, there are certain rules to be respected as well. There are certain rules concerning observable and non-observable targets and the way they are supposed to be destroyed as well. These rules are very clear about the way you are supposed to proceed. I think that it is in everybody's interest in a situation like that, that every possibility should be considered to find an observable target. And, therefore, to -- the quantity of ammunition to be used and also to reduce a number of casualties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am wondering if it is a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is approximately time for the break. Mr. Stamp, how much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I expect approximately half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Half an hour. May I make one comment in view of some guidance, for, if there would be any other expert who would like to change some of the words in his report. It took us 45 minutes to go through a lot of details which were, as far as I can see now, mainly positions in expressions, rather than a change of the report itself. If the Chamber would have been provided with an adapted version, and the same, of course, for the Defence, then you could have asked on one or two issues, for example, delayed fuse, time fuse, why he changed the word. That would have taken 10 to 12 minutes. Now we really lost half an hour and I can assure you that you still missed a few ones as well. We adjourn until a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving you the opportunity, Mr. Stamp, to resume the examination-in-chief, Mr. Ierace, I am glad to see that you are back and that there is no further reason for your absence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. At some time convenient to you, I could attend for the purpose of tendering the exhibits in respect of General Van Baal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, they are all under seal, so I would rather continue with the examination of the witness rather than ... If you would be warned by one of your colleagues when we come to that. It might not be until the next break, certainly not. And there is no urgency in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the conclusion of the examination-in-chief or the witness's evidence altogether, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's try to do it five minutes before the next break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a question and you will answer -- may I ask, would you order the firing of a large quantity of artillery rounds into unobserved areas of a city with a large civilian population inhabiting there?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: You have got to know all the circumstances. So I don't think that I would be able to give you a concrete answer based on the information that I have just been given. I think, however, that you've got to be extremely prudent and every single time when there might be civil casualties due to artillery, you have to be extremely prudent. At the same time, you have to try and use as little ammunition as possible. So this should be the decision of the commander. And the only way you can reach this decision is to try and have a fire effect on the target on the circumstances where the target is observable. Now referring to your question, reconnaissance has to have very accurate information and data about the location and the nature of the targets. The objective should be to fire as accurately as possible. This is what I would consider correct, professionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. May I take you to that part of your report where you speak of the tasks of artillery fire and that is at page 2 of the report. Here you have referred to the task of artillery fire in terms of its effects on what you call, "targets." And you refer in bold close to the bottom of the page to "disturbance" with "wear out" in brackets, and you describe what that is. Can I ask you, in artillery terminology, is there another word for that type of fire at targets.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me, I did not understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In artillery terminology, is there another term for what you have here described as "disturbance" or "wear out"?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. There is another term for describing this kind of fire. In the terminology of the artillery, the term which is used is, "harassment." Basically the contents are the same. It is a synonym, but the term the artillery would use would be "harassment".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you close that paragraph by saying and I may quote: "Its use against a civilian population not in uniform and proven to be unarmed is not a legitimate and planned military assignment."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, I think that this is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In ordering the fire of artillery on areas or targets where civilian casualties are possible or probable -- I withdraw that. May I rephrase it? If civilian casualties are possible or probable, on what authority could an artillery crew commander order fire onto that area where there are civilians?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: I think I need some clarification concerning the question because I don't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where an artillery battery commander is aware of the possibility or probability of civilian casualties occurring from a fire mission, on what authority could he, in standard artillery usage, order the fire or would he have to refer to someone?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I understand the question. If we are talking about a commander of a battery, you have to know that a commander of such rank is not supposed to take such an important decision. If a battery commander is aware of the fact that in the area he is supposed to fire at is like that, he has got to inform his superior about that fact. So his superior is supposed to be informed in a way because we can't suppose that he is capable of observing or looking at that area with his -- by his own means. And I think that from there on, this is not the battery commander's responsibility. It is not his responsibility, whether he is going to execute the task he is supposed to. If he does execute the task after his report, once he has already informed his superior, I think that the question of responsibility is not at the level of the battery commander any more. This is a general answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to turn very briefly to some comments you made in your report on the issue of accuracy, primarily the observations which you make from page 5, the second to last paragraph of page 5, to page 6 of your report. May I first ask, in conventional artillery usage and operation, are artillery pieces normally left to remain in a single firing position after each fire mission or is it otherwise?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Could you please specify your question if possible. I don't quite understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the standard operation of artillery in combat, do they normally execute a fire mission and remove from the spot where they fired or do Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. they normally remain in the spot where they fired from for a long time in the course of this standard procedure for artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Thank you. In general, my answer would be the following: By and large a subunit in artillery, once the mission has been carried out, would leave the spot, the firing spot, the firing position, from which it had fired the artillery, the shells. Precisely, for the following reason: In every single case when the enemy artillery is present, as well, they can expect a riposte retaliation. So it is in the very obvious interest of an artillery unit to leave the spot as quickly as possible after the mission has been carried out. And, of course, this has to be done prior to the reply by the enemy artillery, obviously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Having regard to your answer, can you comment on this passage on page 6, the penultimate paragraph of your report. "An artillery piece and the mortars laying siege to a city --" I will start again. "An artillery piece and the mortars laying siege to a city have good opportunity to transfer the fire from the ranging fire base point where they have probably remained in a single firing position. They knew the ranging fire characteristics of numerous targets that had already been demolished and therefore they were able to perform fire transfer within the specified deadline in a manner that meant the first or only shot impacted into the target with great accuracy without any previous range in shots and therefore completely unexpected." In the context of your previous answer and that passage, could you explain or elaborate a little further on what is meant by "the transfer of fire."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. As I mentioned before, in a basic situation, this is exactly what happens. After the strike, after the shelling, the artillery will leave the firing positions and within the dynamics of the combat, they will move to a couple of hundred metres away from that spot, and that is exactly where they will occupy another firing position. Now, in extreme cases something else can happen. If they don't have to worry about a riposte, the enemy striking back, and also they don't have to worry about the enemy reconnoitering the exact firing spot, it might happen that they maintain the same firing position and they will continue and they will continue carrying out further shelling missions from that very spot. And then, of course, this will be a more favourable situation for them because if we consider carefully, then, of course, targets were not moved, the firing position for fire command were not changed, which means that they can exclude a great many factors and changes which might render the firing mission less precise. And what I describe in this particular paragraph and in answer to your question, we are here talking about a method whereby our shelling can be determined. It is a methodology and if this is a rather precise method, which can be employed in certain target areas, in which that particular unit, artillery unit, had already carried out some missions. And in such situations and from certain points of view, it is easier to determine certain elements regarding the target than in another situation. So in this particular situation, it is possible to employ ranging fire base point and then you can also move your firing position from a ranging base point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean move the position from which you fired or position that you fired at?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: No, no, this is not my idea. Okay. Let's suppose that a target has already been found. Okay? Let's say 20, 30, 40 minutes ago, the target was hit. And then, of course, I know the parameters, and within certain limits in time and space, I can apply the necessary corrections, and thereby, my firing shelling power will be much more precise. And then, of course, it would be much more precise than if I had to fire on a so-called "fresh target." This is the way I understand my answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You refer in your report, and I would like to take you to that area now, to the crucial issue of record keeping. For example, if I could take you to page 8, at line 13, line 13 from the top you say "the specified targets must be recorded in writing at the level of the battery or regiment commander." And at page 11, line 13 from the bottom or line 14 from the bottom, you say, "from the cannon or mortar commander level, every platoon, battery and the division is supposed to record the characteristics of each target shot at so that an investigation, provided it is initiated, can clear any suspicious cases. That is, the latter citation was page 11 and starting at line 14 from the bottom. If upon complaint the targets which are not military targets are hit, would an investigation, if initiated by a commander, be in writing as well?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If upon complaint or if there is a complaint or many complaints of artillery fire striking targets which are not military, and if an investigation is initiated by a commander, would that investigation be in writing as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is a purely theoretical question. Does it concern the whole army or is it directly related to the ARS or the BH army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is a general question put to an expert witness. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you expect that investigations of complaints of non-military targets or civilians being hit by artillery fire be conducted in writing? That basically is the question.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. My answer would be the following: In fact, at every single level, as regards military command in the artillery, it is compulsory to draw up a number of documents, because it is not only prior to artillery fire attack, but also after such an attack, it is necessary to be able to check, to examine the activities. So every single shot fired has to be recorded, and this is precisely why, if there is any kind of accident, let's call it an accident, happens to take place, then we can follow and find out exactly who made that mistake. And, of course, I would like to point out that the possibilities of making mistakes are absolutely vast. And in my opinion, for a commander at a certain level, and let us remain in a general category, if a commander, if such a commander in general learns that an accident has taken place which was caused by the artillery misfiring, then, of course, they have to investigate it. And the investigation does not have to be ordered, necessarily, in writing. At a certain level, a commander can order such an investigation orally or in writing. And it is my conviction that after the investigation, the report which will be received by the commander at a certain level concerning the results of the investigation, then it is my conviction that such a report has to be drawn up in writing. Naturally, what I am saying now, is in answer to your question and I am answering your question in general terms, and of course I don't have any further information in this particular matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just have a moment to confer with my learned friend, just one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is the examination-in-chief. May it please you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Kovacs, you will now be examined by counsel for the Defence. May I take it, Ms. Pilipovic, that you are the one who is examining the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but with your permission, if there is time, my colleague will also ask some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You know the conditions, within the time limits set. And that is half --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, thank you

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Kovacs. Mr. Kovacs, can you tell us if you wrote your report on the basis of your theoretical knowledge?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Do you mean, do I have theoretical knowledge?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, the Defence understands that you do have such theoretical knowledge in view of the titles you have.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, you are absolutely right. You understand it correctly. I have both a theoretical and practical knowledge regarding artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacs. The knowledge that you acquired during the course of your career and training, could you confirm to us whether you also applied this knowledge to the situation in the city of Sarajevo in 1992, 1994, at the time when you wrote your report?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: The knowledge that I have, that I have gleaned from my experience, and my expertise which exist both from the theoretical and the practical standpoint, well, of course, this is the kind of knowledge that I applied, that I used when I wrote my report, my study.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Kovacs, you are confirming to us that you applied your knowledge to the city of Sarajevo, specifically, at the time when you wrote this report?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: When I wrote my report, I did not write it about the city of Sarajevo. It was a general application of artillery or rather the general application of artillery in a combat involving cities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacs. Mr. Kovacs, can we agree then that all the questions that we will touch upon here are questions which are theoretical questions and assumptions and hypothesis, since you were not familiar with the situation in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: I would like to answer the following: Whatever I described in this particular report refers to the general application of artillery. And I don't have and I didn't have at the time any specific information which would have applied to urban warfare in one particular city or town, i.e., the siege of any given town or city, and this is why it is obviously true. You can apply it to Sarajevo, or you can apply it to any other city as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, can you tell us if you have been to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: No, I have never been there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you were preparing your report, did you perhaps study the geographic location of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: As regards Sarajevo, I had the following information. In fact, I had the information that I obtained myself during this particular study, and my studies. And I also had a number of pieces of information which I obtained from the media from different sources of information. Whatever I could obtain, whatever I could find out, in general. I have not studied specifically the very structure of the town, the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, in your report on page 1 of the English text, you speak about observable and non-observable targets. Will you agree with me when I say that under the conditions of war waged in an urban environment, there are many more targets which are not observable?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: This is very general way of describing the situation, so I cannot really agree with you. Because every time you have a situation, every time you have a number of targets, be it in a city, in an urban environment or any kind of built-up environment, you have to make a special effort to observe the targets and to observe target activity for various reasons. But one of them is precisely to attain a certain level of fire effect, fire power. And in a given built-up area, it is precisely the geographical situation of that area that might determine whether you observe your target with optical instruments from a helicopter or using other tools, other methods of reconnoitering, and also it is important to find out to what extent this can be done, using the different methods and instruments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kovacs, when you speak about the targeting of non-observable targets, in order to achieve accuracy when firing at such a target, do you think that one needs a larger quantity of ammunition for that, compared with the quantity of ammunition needed to fire at the observable target?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: This is not my opinion. This is -- were known by the people who write the rules and regulations and use artillery and who are experts in this field. And I think that they have carefully studied these parameters, these situations. And I believe that every military, and especially if we are talking about artillery officers, commanders, I think it makes it very obvious for these people that when they fire at observable targets, then, of course, they will use much less ammunition than if they were firing at non-observable targets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Kovacs, to fire at non-observable targets, one needs much more ammunition in order to improve the accuracy, to be accurate?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: I -- there is something I would like to correct, if you allow me. It is not for added precision that we need more ammunition, but in order to obtain the desired effect and they are not necessarily identical, these two phenomena.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacs. Mr. Kovacs, can you agree with me that in a city it is permitted to fire at non-observable military targets -- at the targets of military targets, observable military targets?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific, because I don't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, can you agree with me that in a city, it is permitted to aim at and fire at non-observed military targets?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: I would like to give you a general answer. In a city or in any kind of settlement there might be observable and non-observable targets. The fact that there is going to be firing at a non-observable target with large quantities of ammunition will depend on the decision taken by the commander in charge. That particular commander has to take the decision whether firing should take place or firing should be targeted at these targets, that is, non-observable targets. The commander has to decide whether it is going to fire or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am not sure if the witness finished his answer. I don't know, perhaps he could indicate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just finished the answer. This was my last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, but my question was whether it is permitted, whether it is allowed in a city to aim at and fire at non-observed military targets. Can you answer, yes or no, if you can, that is?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: No military rules will make a difference, in this respect, whether non-observable targets can be found in cities or out of cities. I would just like to repeat, this is the decision of the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are confirming to us that it is permissible?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: This is not what I said. What I said was that the commander has to decide. This is my answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacs. Mr. Kovacs, on page 1 you spoke about targets, single targets and grouped targets. According to you, in case of a war in a city, is it allowed to aim and fire at single military targets?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: So your question is whether you can fire at single and grouped targets as well?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, I asked you first about single military targets, therefore machine-guns, snipers, mortars. Is it permitted when a war is waged in built-up areas?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Well, my question -- my answer to this question is that you can fire at single targets as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, you spoke to us about grouped military targets. Now, in line with the division that you made, could you perhaps give us a list of the targets which, in your mind, could be defined as grouped military targets?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Of course, I can give you examples, if you would like me to. For instance, as regard single targets, a mortar, one shell or, for instance, a tank piercing gun. As regards grouped military targets, for instance, a platoon with mortars, with three mortars, would fall into this category, gathering infantry or a defence post would just be a few examples because there are quite a lot of them so maybe I wouldn't go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, when you answered my question about whether it was permitted to target and fire at non-observed military targets, you said that it was the commander who decided whether to do it or not. Can you tell us who decides on the use of artillery at a battalion level?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific about your question? Are we talking about the artillery, a special division of the artillery now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Within a battalion.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: The unit commander in the artillery has always a mission, and this mission is given to him by the other unit above him. This mission can be Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. given to him from two directions: His direct superior, artillery superior and the other commander in charge of all the units, the direct superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacs. Mr. Kovacs, on page 1 of the English version under item 8, you divided the targets by their level of cover; you divided them into covered and uncovered. Could you please list the uncovered targets or open targets in city circumstances or city conditions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we just get exactly where we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it is the last one. It is not numbered 8, but it is the 8th linear of this first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, 8th paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In the document I prepared I have already given a few examples of open and covered targets. Basically the simplest way of distinguishing between these two is to say that open targets can be found without any special technical efforts. So they are not, let's say, "dig in." There are no protective facilities surrounding them or covering them. They cannot be found in special combat vehicles. And when we are talking about covered targets, obviously, we have got to mention the opposite case. Let me just give you an example for each. An open target could be, for instance, one mortar which is not in a firing post which has been prepared in a kind of technical way. Or, for instance, an infantry which can be found -- which cannot be found in a kind of building or construction. Another example for covered targets would be an infantry which can be found, for instance, in a building or in a protected facility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, did I understand you correctly that all buildings where troops or army equipment is located in conditions of a city, in city circumstances, in your opinion are military targets, covered military targets?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: No. I think this would be a general way of putting it. It is far too general to put it, because you can't really know this exactly as long as you don't have exact data of reconnaissance, and this information should be in the possession of the commander. And the commander should be aware of the fact that this is a military target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacs. Thank you, Mr. Kovacs. I understood your answer, but my question was whether a building or a house which has soldiers in it in city circumstances, in your opinion, is that a covered military target?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
