utterances.text: Well, I think this depends on the kind of construction or the kind of building we are talking about. If the building in question is capable of providing cover or shelter against an artillery attack, for instance, this could be a covered target. But I think that here again we have got to be very prudent and we have got to examine everything in detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, could you confirm to us that in order to destroy covered targets, it is necessary to use a larger amount of ammunition from the one that would be needed for uncovered targets, for open targets?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific about your question? Do you mean to ask whether more ammunition is necessary for a covered target than an open target?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: In that case my answer is obviously, yes. You need more ammunition in that case, but obviously I would need more information so that I can be more specific in my answer. But in the first approach, I would say, yes, more ammunition is needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacs. Mr. Kovacs, on page 2 of the English version under item 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6, you describe, if I understand you correctly, the tasks of artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, is it permissible to use any of the each individually listed task within the artillery fire that you have listed here in urban conditions of war?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: As regards the artillery, and as regards the task of artillery fire, there is no difference between urban warfare or open space warfare. So obviously all the tasks I have enlisted here are to in both case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacs. Mr. Kovacs, on page 4 of your report, paragraph 2, you speak of the element of surprise. You say that the moment or the element of surprise is of greatest importance when mobile targets are targeted and live forces.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Obviously this is true. The unexpected nature of artillery fire is always one of the basic conditions, the requirements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacs. Mr. Kovacs, would you agree with me if I put it to you that a mortar or mortars that are active from a truck or from another vehicle, that is, as mobile technical equipment, when they are active from inside the city towards enemy positions, in your opinion, such mortars do they represent a legitimate military target?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Could I please ask you whether you mean a mortar which has a mobile carrier?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: In this case, the mortar mounted on a mobile carrier can be considered as a mobile target in the sense that once it has fired, it can quite easily move away from its firing position. But it is not a mobile target because it does not keep moving since one of the specific natures of a mortar is that it can only fire once it is stable, so it is not moving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Mr. Kovacs, if a mortar is placed on a vehicle, on a carrier, on a mobile carrier, and that at one moment it is fired from one position and then that vehicle leaves that position which was used as a firing position, at the moment when it is fired, when the mortar is fired, the mortar which is mounted on a vehicle, in your opinion, is that a legitimate military target?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Well, my question is whether we could be more specific about this? When do you mean this would be a legitimate target, once it is in its firing position and it is firing?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the moment when it is standing in its position and at the moment when it is firing, that is, throughout, always.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: In the moment when it is firing and when the other party is firing back, it could be considered as a legitimate military target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, when such mobile targets are fired on from the side, which is returning fire, which is riposting, would you agree with me to consider that in such a situation, it is possible to open fire on other targets, too; that is, what is the possibility of being accurate in your opinion when fire is open on such a mobile target?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: This depends on the other side, on the other side which is firing back, that is, at this mobile target. So this depends on what kind of means the other side is using to fire, whether the other side is using a cannon, a mortar, or any other ways of firing. This is another approach.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, could you tell us what is the probability of hitting such a target with one shell?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Could I please just ask you just one question, because this is very important? Now, we are talking about weapons at our disposals that we would like to use to hit this target. What kind of weapons do we use or would we like to use?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking specifically, say, about a mortar.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, that's more specific. With a mortar, it is impossible to fire at a mobile target. With a mortar, you would only fire at a target which in the moment when you would like to destroy that particular target is not moving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs on page 4, paragraph 4 of your report, you speak of using mortar shells, that is, with projectiles assembled with explosive uses are used to destroy live forces --

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: I am sorry. I can't really find this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I could assist you, it is on page 4, the 4th paragraph, the third line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 4(a), in fact.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please read out the first few words of the sentence so that we can find it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is "projectile assembled with explosive fuses."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Used for the demolition of the enemy's life forces, weapons, artillery batteries, armoured combat vehicles, radio and radio stations, and vehicles located in open fields --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we have some confusion. When referring to this paragraph at first instance, mention was made of "projectiles assembled with explosive fuses are used to destroy life forces." That is not the part you are quoting now. That is the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It is actually a paragraph before this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we now are concentrating on "projectiles assembled with instant fuse are used for the demolition of the enemy's life forces." Yes, that part we are dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kovacs, we read out or quoted a part of -- section of your report, when you spoke about projectiles with instant fuses and we quoted what they are used for. Could you confirm to us that this is accurate, that this is so?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: You mean to say is it correct, whatever is written in this particular paragraph; is that your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: I haven't changed it today. I didn't find any mistakes here, so I consider this to be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you, Mr. Kovacs. Mr. Kovacs, could you tell us whether the body of a shell, the stabiliser or some other part of such a shell could penetrate into the ground, presuming that it is directly hit the ground?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Please bear with me. I would like to ask you to be kind enough to specify your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you asking me whether from the body of the ammunition, the stabiliser and in this particular case we are talking about a mine, you know, from a mortar or a rocket from a mortar -- shell from a mortar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may I ask you --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are talking about a mortar. We are talking about a mortar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the question seems -- was not entirely clear to the witness. It was not entirely clear to me as well. Would you please think over the formulation of the question during the break because we said that we would spend the last five minutes before the break to deal with the documents. And we have to do that in closed session. Dr. Kovacs, we will have a break for -- until 5 minutes past 6.00. May I ask you to leave the courtroom. You will be escorted out by the usher, because we have to deal with one procedural item that has got nothing to do with your testimony, and we have to do that in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, the Registrar informs me that it might not be necessary to go into closed session, if she deals with the documents in the general description she usually uses.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I indicate at this stage that the only document I seek to formally tender is P2380. The rest have gone into evidence in the usual way by the relevant parts being quoted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Defence has tendered one exhibit and that was not a protected exhibit in whatever way, I think. Am I correct? The witness statements -- or you say we don't have to tender that because -- I think the relevant part has been read out as well. So if you would refrain from tendering it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was D141, which was, in fact, read out. And your question was to find out if we are going to tender it as our exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the first question was whether there was any protective element in it. Of course, the Chamber would not know. And the second question was, since it has been read out, the relevant part, whether you would tender it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no. My other part of the answer, would be why not? We have done the work and I suppose it wouldn't hurt for you to have it before you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it doesn't hurt at all. On the other hand, we of course try to reduce the number of documents we have. But I do not mind. I take it, Mr. Ierace, that -- yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the tender for the reason that has been made clear. The relevant part has been put to the witness, and his has been asked if he agreed or disagreed. Tendering the relevant part of the statement of someone who, I think, is now deceased is inappropriate. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it add anything if it would be tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no point in sacrificing anything for time, Mr. President, which means clearly that we can withdraw that piece from being tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the only document then remaining is P2380 which would be, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Outgoing code cable R004134.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Therefore, it is admitted into evidence. We will adjourn until 5 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I didn't have time to phrase the objection that I was going to make, but on the basis of the same principle, that the one that Mr. Ierace wanted to have applied here, it should be also here that the rule goes for them as well. A lot of things were tendered and some, the same thing is valid for them as well. Thank you in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you wish, Mr. President, I can quickly explain the difference in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have to -- did you check exactly -- let me first have a look at the document and see whether I can find it. No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I could do it obliquely by saying that attached to the cable is the two-page document, the detail of which it is appropriate to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will give a decision on that after the break. We will adjourn until 5 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I promised you a decision on the objection. I will not give it now. The Chamber has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The practice in this Chamber has been not to tender any document of which a part was read, if that part would be the only relevant part of the testimony, that is a matter of practice. That would not mean if some party would insist on tendering, that we finally would say no, but it is very practical to do it the other way. We will have a closer look and compare the two documents. Mr. Piletta-Zanin said that he would not tender his document. Mr. Ierace said that one of the documents he would like to tender. We will have a close look at it, and in line with what I said before, we will then consider whether it would be appropriate to try to convince Mr. Ierace not to tender it or that the Chamber would see such a difference that the Chamber would just accept that the document is tendered and we will give a decision on the admissibility of the document. So I would like to make the parties a clear distinction between the practice in this Court and the rules. We could now continue with the examination of Dr. Kovacs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Might I be excused for the remainder of the session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, it is my duty to clarify the question that I asked you before the break. To enable you to answer this question, I will first ask you something else. Does a shell, and I am talking about a mortar, say 120, when it hits the target, because of the action of the fuse, whether instant or Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. timed, it then explodes, does it?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Well, if the mortar shell hits the target then the likelihood that it will explode is very great indeed, if that is your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was, yes, Mr. Kovacs. And when it explodes, parts of the shell are dispersed, that is burst, and a part of the shell which does not burst such as, for instance, the tail-fin, the stabiliser moves with the shell?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Could you please specify your question? Do you mean to ask about what happens after the explosion of the shell, just what exactly is going to happen to the tail-fin? Is that what you want to know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, that is what I wanted to ask you.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Well, it is very difficult to say anything in general terms about this matter because that depends on what kind of land, what kind of soil, what kind of ground the explosion takes place on. Because when you talk about the tail-fin, after the explosion, generally the tail-fin would continue the trajectory in direction of the ground. Now, whether after that the tail-fin will remain in place, i.e., in the crater, for instance, or else whether it will continue further, I mean, this is very difficult to answer, to give you a straightforward answer, because both cases are possible. Now, the only thing that I could render more precise in my answer would be this: If the ground is soft, then in general you would find the tail-fin close to the place where it first hit the ground. But as far as the bounce back is concerned from the ground and the direction into which it would continue, well, this is something that nobody could foretell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we were speaking about conditions. Can the tail-fin then penetrate the ground, bury itself in the ground?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: If your question is whether the tail-fin, after the explosion, would penetrate into the ground, well then my answer would be that this is quite possible. It can happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can that happen in case of an asphalt or a macadam ground?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: In this particular case the main point would be to find out whether the macadam or the concrete is thick enough. You would have to know the exact thickness. If there is a layer of concrete which is very thick, then obviously the tail-fin would bounce back. Now, if there is a thin layer of asphalt, then, of course, the pieces of the tail-fin could go through and penetrate it. But, of course, it is not only a question of the quality or the characteristics of the ground, but also it is a question of the angle of impact and there are a number of other factors that you would have to take into account.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when you allowed that one had a thin layer of asphalt, that is, the situation when you say it can penetrate the ground, how deep can the tail-fin of a shell of 82 or 120 millimetres, how deep into the ground, how deep can it penetrate the ground?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: To this question, I would like to answer the following. I am now referring to the first part of your question. In my opinion, if there is a thin layer of asphalt, and of course I don't know the exact thickness that you are referring to, but theoretically that can be penetrated. Now, to say to what depth it could go into this layer, well, I couldn't give you a satisfactory answer because that is beyond the scope of my expertise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would you say in case of a concrete base, concrete ground? So, say, types of mortars, but hitting concrete?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I object on the basis that the question is imprecise. It is bad because it is vague. The question: "What would you say in respect of concrete ground," is not direct the witness to an issue relevant to the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has been speaking about concrete ground already, Ms. Pilipovic. And has told us that it depends on a lot of circumstances. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not quite sure Your Honour, that the witness was precise enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question is, how deep can the tail-fin of a shell coming from an 81, 82 or 120 millimetres penetrate a layer of concrete?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just to add that he answered that question and said that he could not give a satisfactory answer because that is outside the scope of his expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first try to find out whether the expert deems himself enough an expert in the field of the kinetics, because we are slowly moving from expertise in mortars and into kinetics. Mr. Kovacs, you have told us that you could not give us a satisfy answer as far as penetration of mortar shell tail-fins that would go into a tarmac surface because it was beyond your scope of expertise. Now a question has been put to you in respect of the penetration into a concrete area and how deep a mortar tail-fin would penetrate. Would you consider this question one you could answer on the basis of your expertise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot -- I am not prepared from the point of view of my expertise, I am not prepared to give you an answer, a satisfactory answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please move to your next subject, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, on page 5, passage paragraph 3 of your report, it begins with the words: "using the reports of occasional eyewitnesses, conclusions can be drawn about the usage of particular types of projectile." Mr. Kovacs, did you write this on the basis of your theoretical or on the basis of your practical knowledge?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Are you talking about the entire paragraph?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about the first words in this paragraph that you used. "Using the reports of occasional eyewitnesses, conclusions can be drawn about the usage of particular types of projectiles."

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: When I wrote this text, I used my theoretical and practical knowledge to an equal extent because it is precisely because of my responsibilities that I have been able to work with various types of ammunition and I was in charge of organising or supervising the use of these ammunitions or as I saw, I have seen of the way they were being used. And as far as the application of the use of ammunition is concerned, you have certain external indicators and these are indicators, these signs, are visible, relatively speaking, even for non-experts, non-specialists. When you see them, when you notice them, you can draw certain conclusions concerning the type of ammunition that has been used in that particular instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, are you telling us that you talked with accidental passersby about whether they could determine the type of the fired projectile?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: No, no, this is not at all what I was saying. I was talking about the fact that when you have seen certain types of ammunition being used as an eyewitness, if you were present, then on the basis of their account of the event, you are able to come to certain conclusions, and you can possibly determine the type of ammunition that has been use.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, in your opinion, would an ordinary person, a layman who is not an expert on weapons, would that person be able to tell by sound which shell is being fired; that is, the shell which is flying by or which has been fired?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: No, no, no, this is not what I am saying at all. I think that when a shell hits the target, there is an explosion, and this explosion has a number of external signs, if you like, external indicators, characteristics, from which you can draw certain conclusions as to the type of shell that has been used. But, of course the ordinary lay person would never be able to determine the type of ammunition that has been used, obviously. But on the basis of certain external signs and on the basis of the account given by the eyewitness, the expert can come to certain conclusions. And of course I am not trying to pretend that the ordinary passerby would be an expert. I am just saying that on the basis of his or her account, an expert can come to certain conclusions. And of course I am not talking about the trajectory, I am talking about the exact impact itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, did I understand you correctly that in your opinion, an ordinary person cannot tell apart just by sound a shell which is flying, nor can that person determine the calibre of a shell at the moment when this shell is fire?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific about your question? Because I would like to know whether we are talking about trajectory here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we are talking about the trajectory, first of all, could you answer in relation to the trajectory?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. You have got to note that the speed of the ammunition on the trajectory is that you can't really see that. There is a sound effect on the basis of which an ordinary lay person or an expert could not specify 100 per cent what kind of shell it was. Because of the high speed of these shells, they are invisible on the trajectory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, we are talking about firing a shell in urban conditions. In your opinion, at which distance can you hear the sound of a shell being fired? We are talking about a 120 millimetre shell or 82 millimetre shell.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Would you like me to talk about the sound of the firing?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The firing of the shell from the mortar.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: The sound of the firing itself can be heard from several kilometres away, and the sound of the impact as well. Obviously everything depends on the weather as well, because these are very important factors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In urban conditions, in built-up areas, you just spoke about the possibility that when a shell is fired from a mortar, is it possible to determine in such urban conditions where this sound comes from, considering that you told us how many kilometres you can hear a shell being fired from?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Would you like me to tell you whether an ordinary lay person would be able to tell you the source of the sound?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, that is what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Well, I think that you can have an approximate idea about the source of the sound because in every big city or large city, there are various kinds of noise, sounds. Even today, if an explosion takes place in a city or if there is a very important sound, we could give you the approximate direction of the source of the sound, provided there is no other shooting or firing at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if we are speaking about a hilly, mountainous area, what is then the possibility of determining the sound?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that I could give you an exact figure about the extent to which this is possible because everything depends on the circumstances. But I think that you can have a very good idea. And I would like to repeat that provided there are no other disturbing circumstances. Obviously it is possible for two or three people to give two or three different directions. But I think that the average man or the average woman could have a fairly good idea about the direction of the firing, approximately, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your experience, did you have an opportunity to speak to the people who would be in a position to give you what they saw, their descriptions, or are you just speaking on the basis of your theoretical education?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: No, I haven't had the opportunity of speaking to people like that. But I have already heard quite a few firing and quite a few explosions. And when I answered your question, I tried to remember my own experience in the matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, on page 8, paragraph 5 of your report, "the artillery fire is controlled from the commander's observation post and the battalion's fire control post." At the end of this report, you also said,, and that is in the line 6. Of the paragraph 5, you say that this also means "that a commandant of an army corps -- you say, "This also means that a commandant of an army corps does not give orders directly to the executive artillery subunit." Mr. Kovacs, could you tell us whether a corps commander gives orders to the subunits to carry out firing?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Could I please ask you whether you mean to say that a corps commander is giving orders to an artillery subunit?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Are we talking about the commander of this unit?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking about a corps commander. You said that he does not issue orders to the subordinate unit, to the subunit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, was your question for more precision in the question about whether the orders would be given to the commander of the artillery unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I would like to know here is who is giving orders to whom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, when you are talking about a commander giving orders to a unit, I think the witness asked further specifications on whether these orders were given to the commander of that unit or to the unit or to members of the unit. Would you please specify.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, does the commander, you said, "Commander of an army corps does not issue direct orders to the executive artillery subunit." Is that correct? Do you stand by what you said? So we are talking about issuing orders to the executive artillery subunit.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. Let us please name the artillery subunit. If this artillery subunit is a battery, the order can come from its direct superior and also from its own commander superior. This is part of the jewel command giving process. Is this is satisfactory answer to the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, could you please answer whether commander of an army corps issued orders to the executive subordinate unit of the artillery?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will -- precise. I will give more precision, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, you are referring to what is on page 8 of the report. I would like to --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it is paragraph 8 or -- it is page 8 where it says: "This also means that a commandant of an army corps does not give orders directly to the executive artillery subunit." That is the line you are referring to. The next line reads: "The tasks to be accomplished by the artillery under normal conditions are determined to the artillery commandant of the army corps by the commandant of the army corps." The witness has asked you to specify a few times. I understood this in view of the specification he gave in the report himself by the line next to the one you repeatedly quoted. Could you please ask the witness in the context of the line you quoted before, an answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, does the corps commander issue orders for firing for his or to his brigade artillery group? Of any brigade?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Do you mean that we are talking about a brigade artillery unit?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: If such unit is a huge unit and a temporary one that may include two or four artillery battalions, and the person giving orders to such unit is the one who is supposed to be the commander of such unit, such artillery unit is supposed to be commanded by a corps commander, say, to enforce the corps or to support the corps, obviously the corps commander is the one to give orders to such unit. If the artillery unit is supposed to be formed differently -- would you like me to finish the sentence?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, let us be precise. Yes, you may finish the question and then I will ask you for a clarification.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: If this unit is not supposed to be commanded directly by the corps commander, the commander which is going to be giving orders to such unit is supposed to give it orders. And here we have to differentiate between the various levels of command. Thank you very much. I have finished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please clarify who is in command of the artillery group within an infantry brigade?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Well, I think we have got to stop here for a minute. I think that certain military terms are not really clear. I don't quite understand the question so could you please specify what you mean by, "artillery subunit" or "artillery group," because these are two different things. And I need the clarification because otherwise I can't answer your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, bearing in mind the country where you come from, are you aware or do you know the terms of the infantry brigade and the existence of an artillery group within an infantry brigade?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS
utterances.text: Yes. It is true that these are terms used in the army of the country I come from, but an artillery brigade is part of the organisation -- excuse me. We just need to clarify certain terms between the two of us with my interpreter. Yes. I think that this is clearer now. An infantry brigade is what we are talking about. It is possible to have an artillery group on a temporary basis, but I wanted to emphasise that this is done on a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. temporary basis only. And this group is going to be subordinated to the infantry brigade. I think that this was an important point to make.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am looking at the time. Perhaps we have another 15 or 20 minutes to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then there might be a need to re-examine the witness and questions of the Judges might be there. And when you say, we would need another 15 minutes, does that mean you or does that include Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would unfortunately have to be absent tomorrow, Mr. President. So in any case, I will not -- I don't mind if we are late tonight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but, as a matter of fact, I think that usually, if we know that we could finish in 10 minutes or a quarter of an hour, I would ask the cooperation of the interpreters. But although I have had some complaints, not specifically from the interpreters, but from other groups assisting us of us going over the time now and then. We will not be able to finish within 10 or 15 minutes, so therefore, we have to adjourn until tomorrow. But we will sit tomorrow in the morning, so 9.00, same courtroom. We will adjourn until then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
